title: APEX: Daily API Loads and Email
desc: What it takes to call an outside API from APEX every day, load a staging table and send an email: the network gate, the privileges you really need, four ways to run it without CREATE JOB, and why email needs a mail server.
points: Toggle privileges and see what breaks
Step a call through the network gate
Pick a post office and follow an email

title: APEX Lab Tour
desc: Follow a click through a first Oracle APEX app: browser, ORDS in Tomcat, the APEX engine and your own tables, plus a settings table, confirmation numbers and public-domain BLS data fetched two ways.
points: Step through five scenarios on a live map
Watch settings and counter rows change
Compare copying data in with asking each time

title: ORDS, Tomcat and APEX Lab
desc: One practice lab in three stages: ORDS by itself, ORDS inside Tomcat, then APEX on top. See where each piece runs, which database account answers each address, and what every error code meant.
points: Step through the three stages on a map
Pick an address and see who answers
Flip four switches and see what breaks

title: ORDS Architecture, Explained
desc: What happens between an HTTP request and your schema: Tomcat, ords.war, the JDBC driver, the connection pool, ORDS_PUBLIC_USER acting as your schema, and how grants reach other schemas.
points: Follow one request through the building
Check the office analogy step by step
Run the pool and watch lines go new and warm

title: ORDS 403, Hardened Grants
desc: Why every PL/SQL handler got 403 on a hardened database while plain SQL GETs worked: the code ORDS runs around your handler needs DBMS_LOB and DBMS_PICKLER. Look inside both packages and weigh the risk of each grant.
points: Trace a request through all five ORDS stages
See what each package does and how risky its grant is
Copy the checks and the DBA request

title: ORDS 403, Explained
desc: Why a REST gateway schema's POST handlers got 403 while GETs worked: the HTP reproduction from the lab, the two packages the real database was missing, and why DBMS_PICKLER is only asked on new connections.
points: Replay the investigation and see why HTP was ruled out
Watch connections go new and warm, step by step
Simulate requests and rebuild the lab
